baseLayer.name: Terrain elevation
baseLayer.attribution: NASA JPL, NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second V001 (doi:10.5067/MEaSUREs/NASADEM/NASADEM_HGT.001); distributed by NASA LP DAAC
limitations: A pre-event surface model from the February 2000 SRTM flight: it does not show changes from the 2026 event, or the 26 years before it.
Gaps in steep terrain and radar shadow were filled from other elevation models during NASA's reprocessing, so heights on the steepest walls are less certain.

layers.name: UNOSAT mudflow/rockflow extent (64.91 km²)
limitations: UNOSAT records this layer as 'Not yet field validated'. Preliminary satellite-based mapping, not ground truth.
Independent of NISAR. Area computed here in UTM 45N from the polygon, because the source's Area_ha attribute duplicates Area_m2.

layers.name: UNOSAT detachment zone (1.96 km²)
limitations: UNOSAT records this layer as 'Not yet field validated'. Preliminary satellite-based mapping, not ground truth.
Source inconsistency: layer name says 26 August 2026 but its SensorDate attribute says 26 September 2026. Treat the date as unresolved.

layers.name: NISAR stability, Track 48 (descending), 2026-08-16 to 2026-08-28
layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
limitations: Pairs are not alike: lengths 12, 24 days and radar modes 2000, 4000 in the file names. Longer pairs and different modes lower coherence by themselves.
One value per pair, nothing interpolated between pairs.
Provisional data.
layers.note: Bright: the ground stayed the same between the two passes. Dark: it changed, or it is water or radar shadow. This pair spans the 26 August event, so a dark patch alone does not say what happened there.

layers.name: NISAR backscatter (HH), Track 48, descending, 2026-08-16
layers.note: Bright: rough rock, debris and slopes facing the radar. Dark: smooth or wet ground, water, or radar shadow. One date on its own: it does not show change.
layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
limitations: A single-date snapshot, not a damage or flood classification.
Covers 44% of the case area: only frame 74 was downloaded, and the product's own mask removes samples that were not fully focused.
40 MHz radar mode, 10 m posting in the file; averaged here to 40 m for the map and 80 m for the inspector, in linear power.
Provisional data.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC

layers.name: NISAR backscatter change (HH), Track 48, descending, 2026-08-16 to 2026-08-28
layers.note: Orange: brighter on the second date. Blue: darker. White: little change. New debris, wet soil, snow and vegetation all change the radar return, so colour alone does not say what happened.
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
limitations: Derived from two dates; the 26 August event falls between them, and so does 12 days of monsoon weather.
The two files use different radar modes (40 and 20 MHz, 10 and 20 m), averaged to the same 40 m grid first.
Only frame 74 was downloaded: 38% of the case area has both dates.
Provisional data.

layers.name: Sentinel-1 backscatter change before the event (control), 12 August to 24 August (OPERA, track 19)
layers.note: Orange: brighter on the second date. Blue: darker. White: little change. New debris, wet soil, snow and vegetation all change the radar return, so colour alone does not say what happened.
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NASA/JPL OPERA RTC-S1 (from Copernicus Sentinel-1 data, ESA); distributed by ASF DAAC
limitations: Sentinel-1 is an ESA mission; NASA's OPERA project made these terrain-corrected images from it. Not a NISAR result.
Both dates are before 26 August: this is the control for ordinary 12-day change.
Layover and shadow pixels flagged by OPERA are left out.
C-band reacts to soil moisture and vegetation more than NISAR's L-band.
layers.maturity: Derived from OPERA RTC-S1 v1.0 (provisional validation)
